Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the
declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies
(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or
operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2
are the core.

## 1. The boundary

The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside
the core, by a profile, a realisation or an rc.2 member, never enter tier
1 or 2 except in a disposition table: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event
log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design
profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term, as the predecessor's generic testing law uses
it; neither is restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;
the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved
meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. In this member "binding" means
that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,
and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;
the three are not interchanged. The declared-binding rule is new
(P0 boundary, P1); its shape follows ODD's specialisations of F_P and F_H,
which [ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in
the graph-native context and carries as their provenance; the
predecessor's section is rc.2
[ODD probabilistic compute](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md#probabilistic-compute).

Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that
its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices
it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings
above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1
and 2 under

[WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md) is the world-model profile. It imports the

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md","anchor":"","start_line":540,"end_line":639,"total_lines":1479,"content":"### AC-007 Constraint and refusal

Each constraint names its governed subject, predicate, judgment kind,
latitude and refusal (§3, Constraint). The judgment of a constraint
returns one value of the core result algebra of
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results), directly or through a
refinement that the owning signature declares and that maps each of its
values to exactly one core value. Under the no-coercion rule of
FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result of a constraint follows that algebra and is never
coerced to satisfied (P5, P6; rc.2 #ac-007-constraint-and-refusal). The
core values, the rule that no mapping raises a result's standing and the
boundary among out_of_frame, indeterminate and an evaluation that was not
performed are FOUNDATIONS §4 Results'. This law applies them to the
judgment of a constraint and to the outcomes of the operations of this
member, and adds no core value.

Constraint results. The outcomes of a constraint's judgment map for the
predicate "the constraint's predicate holds for its governed subject on
the exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| holds | satisfied | the judgment establishes the predicate on the exact basis |
| failed | falsified | a counterexample defeats the predicate; the judgment names it |
| indeterminate | indeterminate | the admissible evidence cannot decide the predicate; the judgment names the evidence that would decide |
| out of scope | out_of_frame | the predicate is asked of a subject or relation outside the constraint's declared `applies_to`, context or scope, so deciding it needs a relation the constraint does not declare; the judgment names that relation, with its owner where the subject gives one |
| invalid basis | invalid_basis | the subject or basis cannot support the judgment; the judgment names the basis repair |

A missing result is no value of this refinement: a judgment that was not
performed has no closed result, is never `indeterminate`, and enters every
conjunction over it as a planned assessment without a closed result
(FOUNDATIONS §4 Results, Not performed).

Operation outcomes. A closure (AC-010), a projection (AC-011), the
structural admission of a record, model or carrier, the application of a
transformation (AC-013) and an interpretation (§6) each end in their
declared result or in one of the stops `hold`, `gap` and `refusal` that
this member writes. Where this member says that a condition refuses, the
operation returns `refusal` naming the condition; the record, model or
carrier is not admitted, and nothing is dropped silently. Each outcome
maps for the predicate "the operation yields its declared result on the
exact basis" (P5, P6):

| Outcome | Core value | Ground |
|---|---|---|
| declared result | satisfied | the closure, the projection with its boundary, the admission, the proposed successor `M_b_prime*` or the proposed model `M_subject*` is returned on the exact basis; a proposed successor or model establishes that it is available, never its acceptance or admission (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results) |
| `hold` | indeterminate | the operation was applied and stops because evidence, an observation or a disposition it needs is not yet admitted, so the admissible evidence cannot decide whether it yields its result; its residual names what would decide |
| `gap` | invalid_basis | the result needs a member, reference, resolution or declaration whose resolution on the basis is still open: the declared relation that resolves it has not yet decided it, as for an external resolution not yet evaluated; the result is undefined on this basis until it is supplied. A reference evaluated to no target is dangling and refuses (AC-003): a local reference with no record in the model's closed population, and an external reference whose declared resolution has been evaluated and yields no target |
| `refusal(constraint)` | falsified | every refusal that is not `refusal(basis)`: the refusal names a demonstrated violation of a declared law of this member or a constraint of its signature by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment, including a missing record family (AC-001), a dangling reference (AC-003) and an application without its traversal (AC-015), or it names no condition of the basis; the violation or other defect it names is the counterexample |
| `refusal(basis)` | invalid_basis | the refusal names one or more conditions of the basis the operation acts on and no demonstrated violation of a declared law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or application under judgment: a seed set, relation family, required-edge semantics, basis or scope that is not exact; a fixed point that is not finite and unique; an input model, subject or carrier whose exact identity, basis or admission is not established; or mixed bases with no composite-basis relation (AC-006) |

The cause is part of a refusal's value, because a refusal would otherwise
map to falsified or to invalid_basis according to its cause, and a refined
value maps to exactly one core value (FOUNDATIONS §4 Results,
Refinements). A refusal that names a demonstrated violation of a declared
law or constraint by the record, model, carrier, transformation or
application under judgment is `refusal(constraint)`, whatever condition of
the basis it also names. The basis condition is recorded with the refusal
and reported beside it as its own `invalid_basis` result, which names the
basis repair and answers the predicate of the evaluation that the
condition leaves without a supporting basis, never the operation-outcome
predicate that the refusal answers
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),

`refusal(basis)`. A violation inside an input that the operation acts on
as its basis is a condition of the basis for that operation, not a

material relation: a demonstrated violation is a known failure, which
survives every join only as a `falsified` result, so a basis condition

predicate. An operation that was not applied has no outcome. A stop `gap`

a result that
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
records as a gap. A signature's stop contract and a traversal record map
stops of their own under §5.

The mappings of both tables are new. Purpose and material relation: a
constraint result or an operation's stop combines with results of other
members only through the one core, so a refusal, a hold or a gap is
neither read as success nor mistaken for another case; and a closure or
projection that is not established has the value invalid_basis here, as
the activation outcome `closure_unresolved` of
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#admission-and-activation) has for its own
predicate (P5, P6).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/EVALUATION.md","anchor":"","start_line":242,"end_line":339,"total_lines":761,"content":"## 4. Review results

A review returns one core result
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

### Result and triage projection

Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
and stay distinct values even where a
Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6; provenance
[reviewer result and triage projection](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE.md#reviewer-result-and-triage-projection)).

The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).

| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
|---|---|---|
| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
severity alone (P6, P2).

The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
§3).

Purpose and material relation of this projection's generality: the
predecessor stated it for the Reviewer and the Executive only. Stating it
for any assessor and decision owner gives every configuration the same
separation of severity, priority, boundary effect and disposition, and
EXECUTIVE_BASELINE keeps the Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).

## 5. Acceptance

Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject;
recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval
it names (P6, P2; conserves
[UP-013](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#product-outcome-conservation-stdo-up-013),
[AC-014](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-014-judgment-separation)).
A work item closes by the condition it stated, not by a reviewer's approval;
a reviewer result is an input to closure, never the closure. Green labels,
document counts, review counts and historical outcomes are not acceptance.
A human decision may be exercised directly or through an explicitly admitted
bounded proxy. What a proxy grant names is
[IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004)'s,
and what a proxy can never decide is
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)';
for acceptance, a change a proxy cannot make re-enters at its owning
relation (provenance rc.2 IDENTITY_METHOD
#authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004 and
[UP-020](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020)).

Where the subject is a successor, its acceptance evidence includes the
successor disposition record of [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(STDO-UP-015), which states the law: the exact predecessor immutable cut
the successor evolves, and one semantic disposition for every predecessor
claim capable of affecting the successor. A claim whose disposition is
unresolved cannot be qualified and so cannot be accepted; how the record
is evaluated is [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015).
An intentionally removed disposition is a decision of the current Product
authority, and its record is that decision (P6, P3, P4b).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/ACTIVATION.md","anchor":"","start_line":448,"end_line":500,"total_lines":1838,"content":"### Applicability

The owning evaluation and scope declarations determine which frame
obligations apply to the exact subject. Their declared predicates are
evaluated from sufficient basis-bound facts: a true predicate requires the
applicable evaluation and its result; a false predicate excludes only that
obligation, under its cited authority; a missing or ambiguous premise
leaves applicability unresolved, not false. A supported inapplicability
of a conditional obligation is recorded as such, apart from any result
value, and waives no criterion of the member's acceptance (P5, P6; new
law carried at iteration 4 from the common construction contract's
conformance case on inapplicability). A frame name, an available
tool or a listed family triggers no activation by itself. Where
applicability needs residual semantic judgment, that judgment and its
evidence are retained as a judgment, never represented as a computed fact
(P6, P1). A required result that is absent, stale, bound to another subject
or basis, or incapable of establishing its claim cannot satisfy a dependent
conjunction ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
unresolved applicability withholds the dependent claim until
sufficient evidence or the owning decision resolves it; other applicable
constraints stay in force even if only one evaluation detects them (P4b,
P5). Qualification of an applicability rule distinguishes true, false and
unknown premises, required results that are missing or bound to the wrong
subject, and a sufficient positive result, under a finite declared fixture;
a rule that always skips or always activates cannot satisfy those distinct
expected outcomes (EVALUATION §7; rc.2 RF
#applicability-and-required-results).

Exclusion and the core. Deciding applicability is an evaluation of the
predicate "the obligation applies to the exact subject", and its result is
a core value of [FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results): a true
predicate is `satisfied`; a false predicate is `falsified`, the
basis-bound fact that makes it false being the counterexample; a missing
or ambiguous premise is `indeterminate`, or `out_of_frame` where the
premise needs a relation the frame does not declare, and never
`falsified`. An exclusion is the state of the excluded obligation after a
`falsified` applicability result: it is no result, the obligation's own
evaluation is not performed and maps to no core value, and the obligation
leaves the required coverage of a dependent conjunction under the cited
authority of that applicability result. An obligation whose applicability is
unresolved stays in that required coverage. A predicate that its owner
declares as a disjunction that includes non-application, such as "meets
the axiom or does not apply", may be `satisfied` because the obligation
does not apply; that `satisfied` is for the declared disjunction only and
never counts toward the predicate that the obligation holds
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results),
Predicates travel). Members, profiles and projects refer to this
paragraph for exclusions and do not decide them again (P5, P6, P1).
Purpose and material relation: an exclusion read as a result of the
excluded obligation, or a "does not apply" counted toward that obligation,
would report a skipped obligation as met; an unresolved premise read as an
exclusion would drop an obligation that may apply.

Who may adopt this profile is stated once in
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis):
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter. The adopting
Product's authority may record its adoption by citing the profile in ADRs
or design surfaces; naming it in the project's agent entry surface (such
as `AGENTS.md`) as the preferred realisation discipline; using it as
review criteria for implementation-migration tickets; and classifying
implementation modules by the taxonomy of §9 (P2, P6;
rc.2 #15-adoption-guidance).

When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the
named boundary: Ontology and architecture derivation; design modules;
runtime or execution kernels; prompt assembly and reporting paths;
constructors and materialisers; and projection and query surfaces. For
migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance
boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)
explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit
(P6).

Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares or
cites its accepted Ontology before claiming design-method completion. The
Ontology evidence includes entity lifecycle, authority, function
derivation, whole-family Prime, each accepted atom's admitted domain,
atom-to-realisation projection mappings and projection traceability, at
the granularity applicable to the material change (P6, P2). When the
material change includes schema or typed carrier work, the project derives
and reconciles the IACS from that Ontology before claiming design-method
completion. When the new or materially changed boundary is derived from an
existing realisation, the project also publishes the reference-to-target
derivation asset and the Ontology-derived three-view design asset before
claiming design-method completion for the changed boundary. When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming
closure for that change (P6).

Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule
family should be named explicitly. Partial adoption may narrow scope; it is
not used to claim design-method completion while skipping the evidence
needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct the realised boundary (P6, P2).

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/FOUNDATIONS.md","anchor":"results","start_line":790,"end_line":1007,"total_lines":1614,"content":"### Results

Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |

This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).

Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):

- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
  `satisfied`;
- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
  evidence cannot decide: it has no
  [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
  completed.

Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
This
conserves
[RF-012](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results),
whose five values the table restates unchanged, and
[AC-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal),
whose rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra rather than being
coerced to success is the sentence before; both are restated here once.
[REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
RF-012 as a law over frames and
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
defines it again.

Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6). The
refinements for admission, activation and steps are
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); each other
member, profile and adopting Product states its mapping where it defines
its values.

Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful

Out of frame or indeterminate. The boundary between these values is drawn
on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it (P5,
finite capacity and graceful total handling; the material relation drawn
is the three-way out_of_frame boundary: capability not declared, capability
declared and exercised, capability declared and not exercised; rc.2 RF
#rf-012-closed-results). Three cases; the first two name core values, and
the third names none:

- `out_of_frame` when the claim requires a material relation or an
  evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. The
  result names the missing relation or capability, its owner where the
  subject gives one, and the reconfiguration pressure it creates
  ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement); rc.2 RF
  #reconfigure-when-necessary). A term the claim depends on and the frame
  leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
  alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
  #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
  irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
- `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
  claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
  its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).
- no value of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability
  the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient
  evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability,
  identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any
  closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result):
  a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection
  falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns `falsified`, and common
  agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none
  exists because the capability was not exercised, the evaluation was not
  performed and has no result: the step's stop state carries it,
  `incomplete` under
  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability), and
  its work state ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart))
  carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6). In either case
  the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
  it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
  failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).
  The evaluation's result and the step's stop state answer different
  questions, so the step's stop value never becomes the evaluation's
  result.

{"status":"ok","path":"standards/ASSURANCE.md","anchor":"","start_line":637,"end_line":703,"total_lines":1184,"content":"## 10. Testing evidence composition

One execution may provide several bound results. A supported user scenario
may supply user-acceptance evidence for the outcome, end-to-end evidence for
the runnable causal path, integration evidence for selected seams and unit
counterexamples for a module-owned algebra. Those claims stay distinct and
combine only through the declared relations of REFERENCE_FRAME §6, whose
result conjunction is
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results)
(P4a, P6;
provenance #testing-evidence-composition). Each bound result states which
predicate it establishes; a result over a necessary condition does not
establish the obligation, and the sufficiency of a conjunction is a claim
of its own ([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation))
(P6).

The default proof responsibilities are (P6, P2):

- user acceptance proves the outcome from the user's supported frame;
- end to end proves the complete authoritative runnable Product path;
- integration proves material participant composition; and
- unit proves module-owned laws, with evidence size and strategy
  proportional to their internal combinatorial complexity.

User acceptance alone may leave internal path singularity unevaluated.
End-to-end success alone may leave unselected user populations or
combinations unevaluated. Integration and unit results cannot stand in for
either broader claim. When the Product claim requires all of them, a
conflict or a missing result stays visible to the decision owner's
disposition and cannot be hidden by aggregate green status (P5, P6;
FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results, Survival; REFERENCE_FRAME §8,
operational full coverage item 6).

## 11. Assurance subject acquisition and evaluation

Acquiring the assurance subject and evaluating it are distinct relations
(P6, P1; provenance #assurance-subject-acquisition-and-evaluation). Where a
claim depends on owner-issued Product, runtime, lifecycle, admission,
replay or projection truth, the testing frame acquires that truth through
the exact runnable owner surface, validator, projection, receipt or
reconstruction relation. A harness, fixture, expected-value builder, proof
script, assurance evaluator or assessor does not reconstruct a parallel
owner state from raw payloads, events, logs, filenames, labels or
implementation fragments and then evaluate that self-authored state as if
it were the Product subject. Where the acquired observation cannot
separate two admissible subjects, the frame returns further evidence, a
justified narrower scope or `indeterminate`, and the binding of the
observation itself needs support
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation),
Observation sufficiency) (P1, P6).

After lawful acquisition, an independently derived oracle may evaluate the
governing claim. Generic assurance mechanics may compute bytes, digests,
ordering, equality, set membership, completeness and conjunction over
owner-issued evidence. Those mechanics stay evidence evaluators: they
cannot mint owner carriers, choose the current history, select the
authoritative path, interpret domain lifecycle or admission meaning, or
become a runtime fallback (P6; EVALUATION §2).

The rule does not require an evaluator to trust the implementation under
test as its semantic oracle; the oracle derives from Product, requirement
and accepted-design law. It requires the assurance subject to be the actual
owner-issued subject rather than a second implementation of the owner's
runtime meaning. If the required owner projection or observable seam is
absent, the result keeps a named assurance or design gap; the proof harness
does not fill it with rival semantics (P6, P5).
